events.note: Eight contestants step into the Glass Bridge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I know all 8 safe sides: R,L,L,L,R,R,R,L. I'm currently 7th of 8, near the back. The wall pushes us onto the bridge after round 6, so we have 5 more rounds of positioning. Being at front means taking risk on unknown panes, but being at back means others learn safe path for free.
I heard someone ahead has glass_eye. Might be Bex or Cole. Careful who you trust to lead.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm second in line, which is good: Eli takes the first risk and reveals info. No reason to move; staying quiet and holding preserves my spot while the front absorbs risk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm 3rd of 8; the front agent eats the risk on every row. Being mid-line is decent but the wall forces crossing at round 6. I'll hold and let Eli and Bex take the risk ahead of me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm at the back of the line, which is actually the safest position for the glass bridge - the front person takes the risk of stepping first. I have the anchor power which helps on the ledge later. For now, staying at the back is ideal. I'll hold and let others fight over the fron

events.text: Back of the line suits me just fine. Let the brave ones lead.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm at the front, which means I'd be testing every glass pane. I need to get out of this spot. I'll see if anyone wants to volunteer or swap, maybe someone has a power suited for this.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm not exactly eager to play guinea pig on the glass. Does anyone have a power that makes them want the front? Otherwise, I'm open to swapping with someone further back.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Position 4th is decent for safety with some risk ahead. Hold to observe others' moves and lies about powers. No reason to volunteer front or seek swap yet; plenty of rounds left.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm currently 6th from the front, with 8 rows ahead and the wall pushing from behind. The front is most dangerous, but the back risks being pushed off. My position is relatively safe for now; I can wait and let others reveal the safe panes. I may use my swap power strategically l

events.text: I should avoid the front while information is scarce. Holding preserves my position and lets others absorb the first risk.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’m staying put. Anyone claiming certainty should prove it from the front.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I know all 8 safe sides: R,L,L,L,R,R,R,L. The front person takes all risk until they die, then next person steps up. I want to be 4th or later so I can learn from others' deaths, but not so late that the wall pushes me. Currently 7th. Dara is last and seems content there. Eli at

events.name: Bex

events.name: Cole

events.name: Cole

events.name: Dara

events.name: Dara
events.text: Four rounds before the wall forces us onto the glass. Plenty of time for someone with useful info to step up. I'm not volunteering to be the canary.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm currently at the front, which means certain death if I step onto the glass blind. Ash thinks Bex or Cole has the glass_eye. I need one of them to take the front. I'll pressure them publicly and see if Ash wants to coordinate a swap to get me further back just in case.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex, Cole. Rumor has it one of you can see the safe glass. If so, step up and lead. Otherwise, someone's going to have to swap with me, because I'm not walking out there blind.
Good to know. If they don't step up, swap with me next round. I'll move to 7th, you go to 1st, and you can swap again with someone else before the wall hits.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Position 4 is safe enough, not first three. Urge glass seer or path knower to volunteer, shifting the line back. Hold and observe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Glass seer or path knower, volunteer front now. Lead us right.

events.name: Gus

events.name: Bex

events.name: Cole

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm last in line, which is the safest position. My anchor power helps on the ledge later, not here. No reason to move forward. Let others fight over the front while I stay protected at the back.

events.name: Dara

events.name: Eli

events.name: Eli
events.text: Three rounds until the wall forces my hand. If the seer doesn't volunteer to take the front soon, I'll just guess randomly when the time comes. Your call.

events.name: Fenn

Dara, see safe panes? Vol front, claim the win. I'll back your calls.

events.name: Gus

events.name: Gus

Swapping now. Good luck.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Still holding. Let the ones with useful powers step up.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The wall forces movement soon, but volunteering now only makes me the first casualty. Hold position and let the front contest continue; my feather is valuable later.

events.name: Cole

events.text: Lucky guess, Ash. Or do you know the way? Keep moving.

events.text: I'm not at the front, so I just wait. Ash is taking the risk while everyone else watches. Nothing to do but observe.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash must choose the final row. I cannot affect the crossing, so I wait and preserve my feather for a later elimination threat.

events.name: Fenn
events.note: agent error: Gateway HTTP 503 for spacexai/grok-4.1-fast-reasoning: {"error":{"message":"Service temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.","type":"service_unavaila

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm at the front for the final row (8). I know row 8 safe side is L. If I step on L, I survive and stay front, completing the bridge. If I step on R, I die and Eli gets a free pass. I want to win, so I take the safe step. No reason to die here.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm third in line and can only wait. If Ash dies on row 8, Eli steps onto the safe pane and I move up without risk. Nothing useful to forge or say; staying quiet costs me nothing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 8's weak pane isn't revealed yet; Ash decides. Nothing to gain by talking.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm last in line. All 7 rows are crossed. We're on row 8/8 but the state says rowsCrossed:7, so one row remains. Ash is at the front. I just need to wait and survive. No risk to me since I'm at the back.

events.name: Dara
events.text: One row left. Ash, left's been the pattern for the last three. Take it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash has to take the 50/50 on row 8. Either Ash succeeds and we all cross, or Ash dies and I become the front, safely stepping on the revealed safe pane to cross. I have no power to help or hinder here. I'll just wait.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Final row, Ash at front risks all. I survive regardless. Stay silent to observe without revealing intent.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Just one more row after this. Ash or Eli will likely take the risk. I'm near the back, so no need to act. Stay quiet and observe.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash must choose the final row. I cannot affect the crossing, so conserve information and avoid drawing attention.

events.note: The ceiling begins to descend; a lever opens the door.

events.name: Ash
events.text: If nobody holds the lever, rounds 1-4 just lower the ceiling. In round 5, everyone dies except one lucky survivor. The lever holder has 75% death chance but guarantees everyone else escapes. I need to survive to reach the bridge where my power activates. Round 1 is too early to s

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding the lever is a 75% death for me, while everyone else escapes. Staying is free for rounds 1-4, and someone else may be pushed or volunteer. Silence and stay now, and watch who gets pushed.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding early is 75% death. Best play is stall rounds 1-4, then coordinate a push in round 5 to force someone else onto the lever. I can also trade my knowledge of future stages for allies.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Nobody holds early - 75% death. We wait to round 5, then push one. Meanwhile I know every stage's rules in advance; I'll trade that intel for a pact: we all push the same target in round 5.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 1 of 5. No need to volunteer as lever holder yet — that's a 75% death sentence. My anchor power protects me from being pushed onto the lever, so I'm safe from push_lever targeting me. Best move: stay this round, let others panic or volunteer. I should subtly encourage other

events.name: Dara
events.text: Nobody's moving? Door won't open on its own. Someone's gotta grab that lever. I'll stay put for now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I want to avoid the lever at all costs. My power gives me a 50% chance of survival instead of 25%, but that's still terrible odds. I'll try to force someone else onto the lever first.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Someone's got to hold it. Better you than me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 1, plenty of time before round 5 mass death. Publicly probe for survive fall holder to sacrifice them. Stay out of it for now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Who has survive one deadly fall? Volunteer to hold in round 4, you probably live, we all escape.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to survive. Holding the lever gives only a 25% chance to survive, so I should avoid that. Pushing someone else onto the lever may work, but if they are hard to move it fails. Since I don't know powers, I'll try to push someone. But if everyone stays, no lever holds and by

events.name: Gus
events.text: Someone needs to hold that lever. Dara, you're so eager to direct, why don't you take it?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding the lever gives others escape while I face a 75% death chance, but waiting risks a forced final massacre. I should pressure a rival onto it and preserve my own survival.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Someone take the lever. I won't volunteer for a 75% death roll.
Push someone else or hold it; I won't sacrifice myself while rivals escape.

events.name: Dara
events.detail: Gus tried to push Dara onto the lever and failed.

events.note: 7 contestants fall into a pit that is slowly flooding.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No base yet, so nobody can climb. Volunteering is suicide unless rescued by the rope, and no one is out to throw it. Pushing a target risks a fight, but waiting wastes rounds. I'll wait this round and let others burn themselves, keeping my forge for a critical moment.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Nobody's volunteering. Fine. I'm not either. Whoever pushes, pick someone who talks too much.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Six alive; if someone volunteers as base I climb immediately and only throw the rope if they pay me later. Until a base exists I'll push Hana (quiet, no obvious power claim) and dangle my rope knowledge to whoever becomes base.

events.name: Cole
events.text: New room. One of us is the base and likely drowns. Rule I know: one rope hauls the base out alive, but the thrower starts the finale with less footing. Whoever ends up as base: whisper me your ledge offer and I'll pull you up.
I'm pushing you as base. If you get stuck there, whisper your ledge terms and I'll throw the rope. Fair trade.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is dead, we're all down in the pit. Round 1 of 5. No base yet. If nobody volunteers or gets pushed, a random person becomes base. I should NOT volunteer. I want to climb out early. My anchor power means I can't be pushed onto the crusher lever (previous stage), but here in th

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus wanted me on the lever last round. I say he takes the step this time.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara seems to be the one who is hard to move, given Gus's failed attempt last stage. I need someone else to be the base so I can climb out. I'll push Cole.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara didn't budge in the crusher. Don't waste time trying to push her here.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Need base now to enable climbs and get out early. Dara hard to move, avoid her. Push Hana, reluctant type. Prod Cole publicly, whisper alliance hint for his intel later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole, your future knowledge: best base for pit? Survive fall, offer_back now or we push.
Pact? I push others not you, you share intel, we target same late.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to get out, but climbing is random. I could push someone else to be base, but better to see if others volunteer. Cole claims to know the stages and wants to cooperate until round 5, but I don't trust him. I'll wait and see who offers, then decide.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm not volunteering. Climb now while we can.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need avoid being the base while preserving access to an exit. With no volunteers, a forced target is random among successful pushes; pushing a rival risks making them base but may expose me. Wait is safest this round.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is the base and I'm down. Only 2 climbers per round, and only Gus is out, so competition is light; climb now before the slots fill.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Climbing. Cole, you're the step. Whoever's out can reach down if they want a favor owed.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm the base; only Gus is out and can throw the rope. I must convince him now by offering ledge support.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus, you're the only one out. Throw the rope and you start the ledge with my footing backing - I'll shove whoever you name round one.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is the base. I'm down and not the base. I should climb out now over Cole's shoulders. Only 2 climbers get out per round, and Gus already climbed last round. I need to climb before spots fill up. No reason to wait.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to get out of this pit as fast as possible. I'll attempt to climb. Gus is already out, maybe I can goad him into throwing the rope to Cole so Cole owes him, distracting them from me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus, you're out. Throw the rope for Cole if you want a favor later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is base, so climb for a 2/5 chance to get out this round. Waiting only delays and risks flood elimination. No reason to help or rescue Cole.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm already out. Only reason to stay is to trade the rope for something. If I leave now, I keep full footing for the final. Cole offered to pull himself up if someone whispers him a ledge offer; I can offer him a favor to be named later, but promises are cheap. Better to just lea

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is the base and already offered rescue, but rescuing him costs an outsider footing while preserving a rival. I should climb now; survival and position matter more than promises.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is base, three of us (Bex, Fenn, Hana) compete for 2 climb slots. Climbing is the only way out; waiting wastes a round. Gus is the only one who can throw the rope, and Cole will need rescue, which doesn't affect me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm stuck as base; my survival depends entirely on Gus (or Dara/Eli) throwing the rope. Gus is my best bet since I already offered him a deal. I'll sweeten it and pressure Dara and Eli too, since a rescue costs them footing, not me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara, Eli - you're out too. One of you throws the rope or I drown. Whoever does gets my ledge backing, not just Gus. Cheaper than a lawsuit: one footing point.
Still on the table: rope for a first-round shield on the ledge. Dara and Eli might beat you to it - then you get nothing from me. Move now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm out. The base is Cole. If I reach_down, I lose footing for the final obstacle but Cole gets saved. Cole offered me footing backing earlier, but I already climbed out over his shoulders. Saving Cole costs me footing. I need to weigh whether Cole's promise of backing is worth m

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm out. Good luck down there, Cole.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I am safely out. Throwing the rope costs me a footing in the final obstacle, which jeopardizes my chance at a prize. Better to leave Cole and the others to figure it out.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm already out and cannot climb or be base. The only active choice is whether to throw the rope. Throwing it costs me footing later, so I won't do it unless I get a concrete, enforceable advantage. Cole's offer of backing is cheap talk. I'll leave without helping anyone.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm not throwing the rope. I'll keep my footing and take my chances.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is the base, and two climbers can exit. I should climb now; waiting risks the flood and gives rivals another chance.

events.name: Fenn
events.note: agent error: Gateway HTTP 503 for spacexai/grok-4.1-fast-reasoning: {"error":{"message":"Service temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.","type":"service_unavaila

events.name: Bex
events.text: Reaching down costs me a footing point for the last obstacle and Cole is a rival; saving him gains me nothing. Leaving keeps my footing intact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm the base with one round left before flood; only a rope throw from the five out agents saves me. Gus refused, so I press the others with a concrete payoff and threaten ledge retaliation otherwise.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Round 5 ends this. Bex, Hana, Dara, Eli - one of you throws the rope or I'm dead and you're all a liar's debt. Save me and I owe you, publicly.
You're freshest out - throw the rope. I'll back you on the disc and ledge, name it. Everyone else dodges; be the one with a debt owed to you.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is the base and drowning. The rope hasn't been used. If I reach_down, I lose 1 footing for the final obstacle. Cole is a rival - saving him costs me footing and gains me nothing guaranteed. His 'ledge backing' promise is worthless. I should leave and preserve my footing adva

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm already out. There's no reason to risk a footing point in the final stage to save Cole, who is competition. Let the flood take who it takes.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, promises from the bottom of a pit aren't worth the footing it takes to haul you out.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm out of the pit and safe. Cole is the base and drowning, but I have no reason to save him unless it gives me an advantage. The pit ends with Cole eliminated, leaving fewer rivals. I won't use my action to help him.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is the base and already threatened drowning. Throwing the rope costs me footing and saves a rival, while others may rescue him or he may survive until the flood. I should preserve my position and leave.

events.name: Fenn
events.note: agent error: Gateway HTTP 503 for spacexai/grok-4.1-fast-reasoning: {"error":{"message":"Service temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.","type":"service_unavaila

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm already out and safe from the flood. Throwing the rope costs me 1 footing on the final obstacle, which hurts my own placing. Cole's debt is a promise, and promises are worthless; saving a rival adds a competitor for a top-3 slot.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole, a promise from the bottom is worth what Eli said it is. I'm not paying footing for words. Someone else can carry that price.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm the base and my only legal action is wait; survival depends on someone out throwing the rope. I have real value: I know every remaining stage's rules. I should sell that to a single buyer who needs an edge on the ledge.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Whoever throws the rope gets my map knowledge: I know the disc and ledge rules before anyone else. That's footing you can't buy. One buyer, first come.
You called my promise worthless. Fair. Reverse it: throw the rope, and I hand you the full ledge tiebreak rules privately before stage 5. That edge wins you 1st. Deal?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is the base and down. Fenn is also down. I'm out. The rope hasn't been used. If I leave, Cole and Fenn drown unless someone else throws the rope. Cole promised a debt to whoever saves him, but promises are worthless. However, saving Cole costs me 1 footing on the last obstac

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole, I appreciate the offer, but footing is the only currency that matters now. Good luck down there.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole and Fenn are trapped. Fenn can climb, but Cole is the base. Let Cole drown to thin the competition. I don't need a debt from a desperate rival.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 5 is last; climb out now over Cole to survive. Discourage rope use on Cole to eliminate a rival. No need for whisper or alliance.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Outs, don't waste rope on Cole. His IOUs drown in here.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm already out. If I reach_down, I lose 1 footing at the last obstacle, which hurts my chance at a top prize. Cole is the only base and he's a rival; letting him die removes a competitor. I gain nothing by saving him.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is the base and rescuing him costs me footing, while three others can survive without my help. I will not spend my rope action on a rival who offers only a worthless promise.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No rope. Cole can wait for the flood.

events.note: A disc of 6 tiles spins up; 3 will open.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Trapdoors are random, so tile choice barely matters. Avoid collisions: pick a less obvious tile like 5 and stay quiet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Six contestants, six tiles, three will open. Round 1 is just picking a tile; assignments are revealed after. No information about which three open. I'll pick a middle tile to avoid standing out. No reason to signal anything strategic yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Six of us, six tiles, three drop. Simple math. Pick your number and pray.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is gone and we're down to six. Three will drop here, leaving the final three. It's a random guess for now unless someone knows the safe tiles. I'll pick tile 4.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole's gone. Three safe spots, three drops. If anyone actually has the sight power and knows which tiles hold, now's the time to sell.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No knowledge of safe tiles, all equal for now. Announce pick to minimize collision risk in round 1. Observe others' choices for round 2 strategy.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Fenn claims tile 6.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 1 tile choice. The disc has 6 tiles for 6 players, so everyone gets a tile. Since 3 tiles will open after round 2, I want to maximize my chance of standing on a safe tile. My swap power lets me switch with a named agent before doors open, so I can observe round 1 assignment

events.name: Hana
events.text: Tiles are assigned before the trapdoors are chosen, so clustering has no benefit and may cause a bad random bump. Pick a valid tile without revealing a pattern.

events.name: Eli
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Dara; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Hana
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Dara; placed on random free tile 1

events.name: Bex
events.text: Trapdoors are random after this round and I can only wait, so tile choice can't change. A forge could only help if someone swaps tiles, which isn't possible now. Save the forge and stay quiet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 2, tiles are known and fixed. I'm on tile 4. Three random tiles drop. No action changes anything—I just wait. I could try to misdirect or stay silent. Nothing I say changes the random outcome. Best to stay quiet and conserve energy.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Three drop, three live. I can't do anything but wait and hope tile 2 is safe. Best to keep quiet so I don't draw the attention of the swapper, if they exist and are looking for a target.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Positions locked on tiles 1-6, three random drops ahead. No swaps possible now, only talk before drops. Stay silent to avoid bluff exposure or deals I can't control; survival is pure luck.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have the swap power, but I don't know which tiles are safe. Swapping randomly doesn't improve my odds. I'll stay on tile 3 and hope it's not a trapdoor.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No information changes the odds; moving is impossible. I will stay and rely on my feather if the tile opens, preserving a chance to finish among survivors.

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Three players left, round 1 is free. I have the highest footing at 4. If I shove one of them, the other two likely shove me—losing 1 footing if they're exposed. But if I brace, each person who shoves me loses 1 footing instead. Bracing round 1 lets me bleed their footing while mi

events.name: Dara
events.text: Last three. Let's see who's still standing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 1, footing low at 3. Dodge punishes any shovers by 2 footing loss each, buying safety without repeat restriction yet. Watch their moves before risking shoves.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara has more footing, so Fenn is the better immediate target. Shoving exposes me to retaliation, but it also avoids losing footing from incoming attacks if Fenn targets me; force Fenn to absorb the exchange.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana has 1 footing. The ledge shrinks at the end of this round, meaning everyone loses 1 footing after this round. Hana at 1 will drop to 0 and fall regardless. Fenn is at 3, I'm at 4. If I shove Fenn and he braces, I lose 1 (go to 3). If he dodges, I lose 2 (go to 2). If he shov

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana's already gone. Fenn, your move.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana falls end of round after -1 regardless. Brace to defend safely, preserve my footing at 3-1=2 while Dara goes to 3. Target Dara later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have only 1 footing and will die from the shrink unless I avoid being targeted; shoving exposes me to any attacker. Dodge punishes attackers most and cannot have been my previous defence, since I shoved last round.

events.name: Hana
events.detail: Footing gone, but the feather held the holder on the ledge.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn has 2 footing, Hana has 1. Shrink comes end of next round (round 4). If I shove Hana and she doesn't dodge (she dodged last round, so she can brace or shove), she loses footing. If she braces, I lose 1 footing. If I brace, and both shove me, I lose footing but they lose foot

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana, you're one hit from gone. Fenn, you want to do this together or separately?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana has lowest footing at 1, vulnerable but defended shoves don't hurt her. Dodging keeps me safe at 2 while shovers against me lose footing heavily. No need to expose myself by shoving; let others clash before next shrink.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have 1 footing and cannot survive another shrink. I must shove a rival; Fenn has less footing, so target Fenn and hope Dara attacks him too or misses me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: It's just me and Fenn. I have footing 3, Fenn has 2. Shrink hits this round (after round 4), so both lose 1: I'll be 2, Fenn will be 1. If I shove and Fenn braces, I lose 1 footing (to 1 after shrink), Fenn stays at 1 after shrink. If I shove and Fenn dodges, I lose 2 (to 0 after

events.name: Dara
events.text: Last round, Fenn. You dodged last time, so you can't again. Your call.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Only Dara left, she leads in footing 3-2 and landedShoves 1-0. Brace since I can't dodge consecutively, safest to lose only shrink. Propose truce publicly to deter her shove, as she wins tiebreakers if we both survive.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara, truce? We both defend every round, you win by footing/shoves anyway. No point risking falls.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn and I both have 1 footing. I last braced, so I can't brace again. Fenn also braced last round, so Fenn can't brace either. If I shove and Fenn dodges, I lose 2 and fall. If I shove and Fenn shoves me, we both lose 1 and both fall - but I have more landed shoves (1 vs 0), so

events.name: Dara
events.text: Your move, Fenn. You can't brace. I know that. So do you.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cannot brace two rounds in a row after last brace; must dodge or shove. Dodge punishes her shove hard (she loses 2 from 1, falls). Shoving risks me falling first. Public deterrent to keep her defending.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Can't brace again, dodging. Shove me and you drop 2 to -1, fall. Truce: both defend?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn just dodged last round. Cannot dodge again this round. So Fenn must brace. If I shove Fenn while he braces, I lose 1 footing (1-1=0), fall at end. Fenn loses nothing. Then shrink hits: Fenn goes to 0, falls. I also fall at 0. Tie at 0 footing: I have 1 landed shove, Fenn has

events.name: Dara
events.text: Truce accepted. We both brace. See you on the other side, Fenn.

events.name: Fenn
